title: Aviation mechanic performance and inspection rules practice questions
description: Practice questions on 14 CFR 43.13–43.17 and Appendix D: performance rules, annual, 100-hour and progressive inspections, Canadian persons.

questions.question: Under 43.13(a), which tools, equipment, and test apparatus must a person performing maintenance, alteration, or preventive maintenance use?

options.A: Only tools the aircraft owner supplies
options.B: Those necessary to assure completion of the work in accordance with accepted industry practices
options.C: Only tools the FAA has calibrated
options.D: Only the tools listed in the pilot's operating handbook

questions.explanation: 43.13(a) says: "That person shall use the tools, equipment, and test apparatus necessary to assure completion of the work in accordance with accepted industry practices."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.13, Performance rules (general) (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: The manufacturer of an engine recommends special test apparatus for a job. Under 43.13(a), what must the person doing the work use?

options.A: Any test apparatus the person considers adequate for the job
options.B: Only the manufacturer's own apparatus, with no equivalent allowed
options.C: Whatever apparatus the aircraft owner provides for the job
options.D: That equipment or apparatus or its equivalent acceptable to the Administrator

questions.explanation: 43.13(a) says: "If special equipment or test apparatus is recommended by the manufacturer involved, that person must use that equipment or apparatus or its equivalent acceptable to the Administrator."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.13, Performance rules (general) (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: 43.13(b) requires work and materials that leave the item at least equal to its original or properly altered condition. With regard to which qualities?

options.A: Aerodynamic function, structural strength, resistance to vibration and deterioration, and other qualities affecting airworthiness
options.B: Paint finish, interior trim, and overall appearance
options.C: Resale value and the owner's preferences
options.D: Fuel economy and cabin noise only

questions.explanation: 43.13(b) measures the condition "(with regard to aerodynamic function, structural strength, resistance to vibration and deterioration, and other qualities affecting airworthiness)."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.13, Performance rules (general) (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 43.13(c), what is the status of the methods, techniques, and practices in the maintenance manual of the holder of an air carrier operating certificate or an operating certificate under part 121 or 135?

options.A: They may be used only when the manufacturer's maintenance manual is unavailable
options.B: They must be approved again by the aircraft manufacturer before each use
options.C: Unless otherwise notified by the Administrator, they constitute acceptable means of compliance with 43.13
options.D: They apply only to preventive maintenance and never to alterations

questions.explanation: 43.13(c) says that "Unless otherwise notified by the Administrator" these methods, techniques, and practices "constitute acceptable means of compliance with this section."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.13, Performance rules (general) (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 43.15(a)(1), what must each person performing an inspection required by part 91, 125, or 135 determine?

options.A: Whether the aircraft, or portion(s) thereof under inspection, meets all applicable airworthiness requirements
options.B: Whether the aircraft can fly until its next registration renewal
options.C: Whether the aircraft meets the owner's equipment preferences
options.D: Whether the aircraft engine starts on the first attempt

questions.explanation: The person shall "Perform the inspection so as to determine whether the aircraft, or portion(s) thereof under inspection, meets all applicable airworthiness requirements".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.15, Additional performance rules for inspections (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: An inspection is one provided for in part 135. Under 43.15(a)(2), how must it be performed?

options.A: In accordance with procedures chosen by the pilot in command
options.B: In accordance with the instructions and procedures set forth in the inspection program for the aircraft being inspected
options.C: In accordance with the procedures used by the aircraft's previous owner
options.D: In any order the person performing the inspection prefers

questions.explanation: If the inspection is one provided for in "part 125, 135, or § 91.409(e)", the person must "perform the inspection in accordance with the instructions and procedures set forth in the inspection program for the aircraft being inspected."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.15, Additional performance rules for inspections (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 43.15(b), a person performing an inspection required by Part 91 on a rotorcraft inspects the drive shafts or similar systems in accordance with what?

options.A: The pilot's preflight checklist for the rotorcraft
options.B: A list agreed between the owner and the person inspecting
options.C: The rotorcraft's most recent flight log entries
options.D: The maintenance manual or Instructions for Continued Airworthiness of the manufacturer concerned

questions.explanation: The person "shall inspect the following systems in accordance with the maintenance manual or Instructions for Continued Airworthiness of the manufacturer concerned", including "The drive shafts or similar systems."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.15, Additional performance rules for inspections (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Before approving a reciprocating-engine-powered aircraft for return to service after a 100-hour inspection, the person runs the engine under 43.15(c)(2). Which pressures does that run check against the manufacturer's recommendations?

options.A: Hydraulic and brake pressure
options.B: Tire and landing gear strut pressure
options.C: Fuel and oil pressure
options.D: Cabin and pitot-static pressure

questions.explanation: The person must "run the aircraft engine or engines to determine satisfactory performance in accordance with the manufacturer's recommendations of" items that include "Fuel and oil pressure".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.15, Additional performance rules for inspections (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: An AMO whose system of quality control has been approved by Transport Canada Civil Aviation approves (certifies) a major alteration performed under 43.17. Under 43.17(e)(2), the work must have been performed in accordance with what?

options.A: Notes written by the aircraft owner
options.B: Any data the AMO's employee considers adequate
options.C: The pilot's operating handbook carried in the aircraft
options.D: Technical data approved by the FAA

questions.explanation: Such an AMO "may approve (certify) a major repair or major alteration performed under this section if the work was performed in accordance with technical data approved by the FAA."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.17, Maintenance, preventive maintenance, and alterations performed on U.S. aeronautical products by certain Canadian persons (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 43.15(c)(3), after which inspections must a person approving a turbine-engine-powered aircraft for return to service first run the engine or engines?

options.A: After an annual, 100-hour, or progressive inspection
options.B: Only after an annual inspection
options.C: Only after a progressive inspection
options.D: Only after the engine has been removed and reinstalled

questions.explanation: 43.15(c)(3) covers approval "for return to service after an annual, 100-hour, or progressive inspection" and requires the person to "run the aircraft engine or engines to determine satisfactory performance in accordance with the manufacturer's recommendations."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.15, Additional performance rules for inspections (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 43.15(c)(2), who must run the engine of a reciprocating-engine-powered aircraft after a 100-hour inspection, and when?

options.A: The pilot, during the first flight after return to service
options.B: Each person approving the aircraft for return to service, before that approval
options.C: The aircraft owner, within the next 10 hours of flight time
options.D: Any person, at any time after the approval is signed

questions.explanation: "Each person approving a reciprocating-engine-powered aircraft for return to service after an annual or 100-hour inspection shall, before that approval, run the aircraft engine or engines".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.15, Additional performance rules for inspections (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 43.15(d)(1), what must each person performing a progressive inspection do at the start of a progressive inspection system?

options.A: Inspect only the engine and propeller
options.B: Inspect only the items due under the first scheduled interval
options.C: Inspect the aircraft completely
options.D: Review the aircraft records, with no inspection of the aircraft

questions.explanation: Each person performing a progressive inspection "shall, at the start of a progressive inspection system, inspect the aircraft completely."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.15, Additional performance rules for inspections (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: For the purposes of 43.15(d)(1), how is the overhaul of a component or system treated?

options.A: It is considered to be a detailed inspection
options.B: It is considered to be a routine inspection
options.C: It is considered to replace the initial complete inspection
options.D: It is considered to be an annual inspection

questions.explanation: "For the purposes of this subparagraph, the overhaul of a component or system is considered to be a detailed inspection."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.15, Additional performance rules for inspections (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: An aircraft on a progressive inspection is away from the station where inspections are normally conducted. Under 43.15(d)(2), an appropriately rated mechanic who performs the inspection uses whose procedures and forms?

options.A: The mechanic's own procedures and forms
options.B: Those of the pilot in command
options.C: Those of whichever repair station is nearest
options.D: Those of the person who would otherwise perform the inspection

questions.explanation: "an appropriately rated mechanic, a certificated repair station, or the manufacturer of the aircraft may perform inspections in accordance with the procedures and using the forms of the person who would otherwise perform the inspection."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.15, Additional performance rules for inspections (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A person performs an inspection specified in an Airworthiness Limitations section of a manufacturer's maintenance manual. Under 43.16, how must it be performed?

options.A: In accordance with any method the person performing it finds acceptable
options.B: In accordance with the owner's written instructions in the aircraft records
options.C: In accordance with that section, or operations specifications approved by the Administrator under part 121 or 135, or an inspection program approved under § 91.409(e)
options.D: In accordance with the most recent practice used on another aircraft of the same model

questions.explanation: The person "shall perform the inspection or other maintenance in accordance with that section, or in accordance with operations specifications approved by the Administrator under part 121 or 135, or an inspection program approved under § 91.409(e)."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.16, Airworthiness limitations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Appendix D: preparation, fuselage and cabin
questions.question: Under paragraph (a) of Appendix D to Part 43, what must each person performing an annual or 100-hour inspection do before that inspection?

options.A: Drain all fuel and oil from the aircraft
options.B: Remove or open all necessary inspection plates, access doors, fairing, and cowling, and thoroughly clean the aircraft and aircraft engine
options.C: Weigh the aircraft and update its weight and balance
options.D: Fly the aircraft to check its handling

questions.explanation: The person "shall, before that inspection, remove or open all necessary inspection plates, access doors, fairing, and cowling. He shall thoroughly clean the aircraft and aircraft engine."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix D—Scope and Detail of Items (as Applicable to the Particular Aircraft) To Be Included in Annual and 100-Hour Inspections (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Appendix D: preparation, fuselage and cabin
questions.question: Under Appendix D, what is the item "Generally" in the cabin and cockpit group inspected for?

options.A: The color and condition of the upholstery
options.B: The number of seats compared with the passenger count
options.C: Uncleanliness and loose equipment that might foul the controls
options.D: Cabin temperature during engine run

questions.explanation: The cabin and cockpit group item reads "Generally—for uncleanliness and loose equipment that might foul the controls."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix D—Scope and Detail of Items (as Applicable to the Particular Aircraft) To Be Included in Annual and 100-Hour Inspections (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Appendix D: engine, landing gear and other groups
questions.question: During an annual inspection, a mechanic finds weak cylinder compression. What does Appendix D then call for in the internal engine item?

options.A: Inspection for improper internal condition and improper internal tolerances
options.B: Approval for return to service with an entry noting the compression
options.C: A repeat compression check only after the next flight
options.D: Inspection of the exhaust stacks in place of the internal engine

questions.explanation: The internal engine item reads "for cylinder compression and for metal particles or foreign matter on screens and sump drain plugs. If there is weak cylinder compression, for improper internal condition and improper internal tolerances."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix D—Scope and Detail of Items (as Applicable to the Particular Aircraft) To Be Included in Annual and 100-Hour Inspections (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: 43.17(e)(1) makes one exception for an Aircraft Maintenance Engineer when approving (certifying) work performed under 43.17. What does that exception name?

options.A: Preventive maintenance
options.B: Maintenance on a U.S.-registered aircraft located in Canada
options.C: Alterations that are not major alterations
options.D: A major repair or major alteration

questions.explanation: A person authorized in 43.17(c) "must approve (certify) maintenance, preventive maintenance, and alterations performed under this section, except that an Aircraft Maintenance Engineer may not approve a major repair or major alteration."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.17, Maintenance, preventive maintenance, and alterations performed on U.S. aeronautical products by certain Canadian persons (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: 43.17(d) lets a person authorized in 43.17(c) perform maintenance including inspections required by § 91.409, with one exception. Which inspection is excluded?

options.A: A 100-hour inspection
options.B: An annual inspection
options.C: A progressive inspection
options.D: An inspection under an inspection program approved under § 91.409(e)

questions.explanation: Such a person "may perform maintenance (including any inspection required by Sec. 91.409 of this chapter, except an annual inspection), preventive maintenance, and alterations" under the listed conditions.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.17, Maintenance, preventive maintenance, and alterations performed on U.S. aeronautical products by certain Canadian persons (as of Nov 4, 2026)
